**Gates on this head:** `l1-face --pr 35950`: 12 items ok, and `all-checks` flagged only for the stale red described in the note below. Check-runs at d508b3a5: 29 success, 18 skipped, 0 pending, and one failure, which is that stale `opened` run of Check Changeset. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both success. GitHub reads `mergeable_state: clean`. Dogfood battery not owed.

**What I checked:**
- **The fix is the right one.** `pr-automation.yml` subscribes `pull_request` with `[opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited]`. `closed` is not in the list, so the only way a closed PR reaches this job is a label or edit event after close. On such an event, `github.event.pull_request.state` is `closed`, and the new first conjunct skips the job. On every subscribed event of an open PR, drafts included, it is `open`, so open PRs keep every run they had. The card's premise is right. #35842's red run 44739836712 is the `unlabeled pm:awaiting-merge` event 32 minutes after its merge, and it logged its own merge commit as the diff base.
- **The expression parses as intended.** I parsed the workflow at this head with the `yaml` package. `jobs.changeset-check.if` is one line: `github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && !contains(…'skip-changeset') && !(github.head_ref == 'changeset-release/main' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]')`. The release-PR exemption keeps its own parentheses, so the new `&&` does not change how it groups. `actionlint` was not run (the PR says so). The workflow did load and run on this head, which a syntax error would have prevented.
- **Nothing downstream depends on the job.** The only `needs:` in the file is `auto-label → pr-size`. A skipped `changeset-check` therefore skips no other job.
- **Pins of the `if:` text.** `git grep` for the label term finds only the workflow and `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs`. I ran `check-expected-skips --roster` at this head. It still reads Check Changeset as the `skip-changeset` opt-out, "plus 2 further condition(s) the recogniser does not read", so the expected-skip classification holds.
- **Other workflows on label events.** `unlabeled` appears in one other workflow file, `publish-smoke.yml`, and only in a comment: that workflow runs on `workflow_run`. `pr-size` and `auto-label` in this file already skip label and edit events. So this job is the only one the post-merge event reached, as the card says.
- **`skip-changeset`.** The only file touched is `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, which no package ships. l1-face reads "no published package touched (unpublished: @objectstack/spec-monorepo)". objectstack-fleet[bot] hung the label at 22:48:14Z, with the route-2 reason in comment 7052499295. No classifier refused it, so it is not a dev's refused label carried by someone else.
- **`Fixes` is right.** All three Done-when items are met: the guard, open PRs unchanged, and no pin owed an update.
- **The body.** One closing keyword (`Fixes #35949`). The other card numbers (#35842, #35857) appear without verbs.

**One note on the red check (not owed):** the `opened` run of Check Changeset at 22:45:24Z is red (job 136617359681), because the label landed about three minutes after creation, outside the settling read's window. The `labeled` run at 22:48:19Z is `skipped`, and it is the latest run of that name on this head, so it is what counts. GitHub agrees: `mergeable_state` is `clean`. a4-A should read it that way at landing and not re-run the red one (a re-run replays the frozen payload, #5580). The fleet's checklist also asks for a skip-changeset comment that carries both the dev's word and the seat's own check. Comment 7052499295 carries one reason. The reason is true, and I confirmed it above.

**Landing:** not governed. a4-A lands once every check is green.

## Contract review — PASS at d508b3a59dad0459ce75f7f8c66a46e73ad68b02

Head-sha: `d508b3a59dad0459ce75f7f8c66a46e73ad68b02`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml + none
Security-touching: yes

Isolated L2 review of PR #35950 (Fixes #35949) on the rules face: the governed path `.github/workflows/**`. Read: the card and its four comments, the PR body, the one-file diff against `main` (7 added, 1 deleted), the check-runs on this head, ruling record 6722205630 and its card #31538, and the logs of the two runs the card cites. Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-20T23:15Z: 29 success, 18 skipped, 1 red (the stale `opened` run of Check Changeset, see ③).

No must-fix, no should-fix. Three nits (N1 to N3) and one landing flag, which is the first item of ③ and the thing to read first.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The expression.** One hunk, in job `changeset-check`: the job-level `if:` gains a first conjunct, `github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'`, under a five-line comment. All four lines of the folded scalar sit at one indentation, so it still folds to a single expression: state is open, AND no `skip-changeset` in the payload, AND NOT (release branch AND release bot). The release-PR exemption keeps its own parentheses, so the new `&&` regroups nothing. Right.
- **An open PR loses no run, on any event.** `on:` is untouched: `pull_request` with opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited. Every one of the six carries the PR object, and its `state` is `open` for an open PR, a draft included; `reopened` is delivered after the transition, and `synchronize` exists only for an open PR. Measured on this head, not only argued: run 44831520471 (this PR's own `opened` event, a draft) evaluated the head's `if:` and ran the job through every step (job 136617359681). Right.
- **`ready_for_review` and `merge_group`.** Neither is subscribed at the base or at the head, so neither reaches this job, and the diff does not change that. `ready_for_review` would carry `state: open` if it were ever added. `merge_group` carries no PR object: see N1.
- **Closed and merged PRs.** On a label or edit event the payload says `closed`, the conjunct is false and the job reports `skipped`. The premise holds in the logs. #35842: its post-merge `unlabeled pm:awaiting-merge` started run 44739836712 about 32 minutes after the merge; the checkout pinned `origin/main` to the PR's own merge commit 9a28a480d2, the step logged that commit as the diff base and counted 0 changesets. #35857: three green runs, then a red one eight seconds after the same post-merge event. Right, within the boundary N2 names.
- **Merge queue: unchanged.** Five workflows subscribe `merge_group` (ci.yml, lint.yml, governed-surface-guard.yml, pr-body-guards.yml, spec-liveness-check.yml); this one never did. `Check Changeset` is not a required context: the live ruleset on `main` (12119582) requires eleven, and it is not among them. So a skipped or absent `Check Changeset` neither satisfies nor blocks a required status, before or after this diff. Nothing `needs:` the job, and no `workflow_run` consumer names PR Automation. Right.
- **Permissions and token: nothing widened.** No `permissions:` line is added, changed or moved (the job block is still `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`; the file has no workflow-level block). No `secrets`, `github.token` or `uses:` line changes. The trigger stays `pull_request`, never `pull_request_target`. The job now starts on fewer events than before. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` is right. The only path is `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, which no package ships, so the diff publishes nothing (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist item 3). The route-2 reason is on the PR (comment 7052499295). No `.changeset/*.md` row is added, changed or deleted, so route 0 does not apply.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` both stand line-initial in the PR body, and both are right: no accept-set, export or authorable key moves. There is no changeset, so there is no second copy to compare.
- One closing keyword, `Fixes #35949`. The card's three Done-when items are met, the first within N2's boundary; no repo check pins this `if:` text (the `check-expected-skips` fixture is a frozen model, compared with nothing).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Landing is Tier H, and two comments here say otherwise.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35950` reads the path under ruling record 6722205630, letter C, and names two C2 triggers: an `if:` changed on a job that already ran, and a changed job that holds a write token. So this PR lands by the maintainer's merge or enqueue, or on an authorized APPROVED review and then the owning seat (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 14). The card's claim comment (7052031713) and the L1 ACCEPT (7052735589: "Landing: not governed. a4-A lands once every check is green.") are wrong on this point and are not to be acted on. No seat readies, queues or arms auto-merge on this PR, and this PASS lifts none of that. State as read: draft, no auto-merge, no review, so nothing has to be undone. The rest of letter C holds: C1, the workflow edit rides its own PR (one file); C3 does not apply.
- N3 (nit) — the PR body's 维护者速读 says 「要你做什么:无。」. Under Tier H the maintainer's approval or merge is exactly what is owed. A body edit, no head move.
- The red `Check Changeset` on this head is the `opened` run, on a payload frozen before the label landed: the label arrived 176 s after creation, outside the 120 s settling window. The `labeled` run after it is `skipped` and is the newest of that name. Re-running the red one replays the same payload and stays red. Not a defect of the diff.
- Dev report: `open_questions` is empty; `security_findings` is none, and I found none. "actionlint NOT MEASURED" is answered by the head's own runs: the workflow loaded and the edited job ran on this head. The three declared deviations (probe-push order, the model-free trailer pair, "Tests" in place of "Evals") touch nothing reviewed here, and the commit carries the AGENTS.md trailer pair.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff holds no query code.
- On the security line above, `yes` is meant: the hunk changes when a job that holds `pull-requests: write` runs. I found no security defect. The value it reads is the platform's own `state` field, used in an `if:` and never in a shell line. A PR author can move it only by closing the PR, which cannot merge while closed, and reopening fires `reopened`, which runs the job.

### ④ Design judgment

`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, judged against the card's scenario and ruling record 6722205630.

- **The guard sits at the right layer and closes the class.** `on.pull_request` has no state filter, so a job-level `if:` is the only place a workflow can decline a closed PR. A change to the fleet's tidy step instead would leave every other post-merge label or edit event red. A closed PR gates nothing, and one that is reopened gets a fresh run from `reopened`, so no stale cell is left behind.
- **It cannot be used to switch the gate off for a PR that can still merge.** See the last item of ③ and the second item of ①.
- N1 (nit) — polarity when the event has no PR. `== 'open'` reads an absent `state` as "skip"; every other unreadable input in this job resolves to "enforce", as its own comments on the label reads say. Unreachable today: the trigger set is `pull_request` only, and widening it is itself a Tier H edit under letter C. `!= 'closed'` would keep the enforcing direction and change nothing for a real PR. Accepted deviation on this head; revisit if the trigger set ever grows.
- N2 (nit) — where the guard takes effect. A `pull_request` run on a merged PR executes at that PR's own merge commit (run 44739836712 checked out 9a28a480d2 as `main`), and GitHub reads the workflow file at the event's commit. So the guard reaches PRs merged after this one lands, and none merged before it. #35842 and #35857 stay red: a re-run replays the same payload on the same commit. A PR already merged when this lands still goes red when its `pm:awaiting-merge` is removed later. The PR body's two-minute check ("on a merged PR, removing a label now leaves `Check Changeset` `skipped`") holds only for a PR merged after it; the body should say so. The first live proof is this PR's own post-merge `unlabeled`.
- After the guard, the newest `Check Changeset` on a merged PR reads `skipped` instead of its last real result. Neutral, and better than a false red. `check-expected-skips` still rosters the name: it reads the label term and counts the other two conjuncts as unread, and the head's lint lanes are green on it.
